style.library.meaning: The product-wide collection of reusable visual, interface and 3D modeling styles maintained directly by users and Agents.
style.library.scope: The style-library route, its application navigation entry, and page title.
style.library.referent: The flat collection of visual, UI and 3D style entries, not a project folder, session, prompt collection, or archive.
style.library.precedence: Top-level product area parallel to composition and interface workbenches.
examples: Open the style library from the application sidebar.

style.entry-create.meaning: Create one persisted style with a name, category, complete design specification, concise prompt summary, and optional reference images.
style.entry-create.scope: The primary creation action and creation dialog in the style library.
style.entry-create.referent: A new style entry whose creator is fixed by the browser or Agent entry point.
style.entry-create.precedence: Creates the entry before optional reference images are uploaded; distinct from editing an existing entry.
examples: Create a UI style with a description and no reference images.
nonExamples: Add another image to an existing style.
Generate a prompt from a style.

style.entry-edit.meaning: Edit an existing style specification, prompt summary, name, category or reference images while preserving its creator.
style.entry-edit.scope: The edit action and edit dialog in the style-library preview.
style.entry-edit.referent: The currently previewed persisted style entry.
style.entry-edit.precedence: Distinct from creating or permanently deleting a style entry.
examples: Replace the overall description and add a reference image.
nonExamples: Change a User entry into an Agent entry.

style.name.meaning: The short management name used to identify one style entry in the library.
style.name.scope: Style cards and the create/edit form.
style.name.referent: The style entry as a library record, not content sent to an Agent when applying the style.
style.name.precedence: Management metadata separate from the reference images and overall description.
examples: Editorial monochrome.
nonExamples: The complete prose description of the style.

style.category.meaning: The single flat classification of a style as visual imagery, user interface, or 3D modeling.
style.category.scope: Style-library filters, cards, and create/edit form.
style.category.referent: One of three style categories: visual, ui or spatial; categories help discovery and do not restrict session binding.
style.category.precedence: A flat category, not a folder, tree, tag hierarchy, or source type.
examples: Classify a photographic treatment as Visual.
Classify a dashboard treatment as UI.
Classify a low-poly modeling specification as 3D.

style.category-all.meaning: Show style entries from all supported categories without a category restriction.
style.category-all.scope: The first item in the style-library category switch.
style.category-all.precedence: A filter state, not another persisted category.
examples: Display visual and UI styles together.
nonExamples: Create a style whose category is All.

style.category-visual.meaning: A style category for the overall treatment of imagery, illustration, photography, or other composed visual scenes.
style.category-visual.scope: Style-library filters, preview-header markers, and create/edit category controls.
style.category-visual.referent: The visual appearance of a picture or scene rather than an interface layout.
style.category-visual.precedence: Peer to the UI and 3D style categories; describes picture treatment rather than a modeling specification.
examples: Low-saturation cinematic photography.

style.category-ui.meaning: A style category for the visual treatment of application and website interfaces.
style.category-ui.scope: Style-library filters, preview-header markers, and create/edit category controls.
style.category-ui.referent: Interface appearance such as layout rhythm, typography, controls, and surface treatment.
style.category-ui.precedence: Peer to the Visual and 3D style categories.
examples: Quiet monochrome administration interface.

style.creator.meaning: The immutable party that originally created a style entry: User for browser creation or Agent for Agent CLI creation.
style.creator.scope: Style-library creator filter and compact entry marker.
style.creator.referent: Original creation ownership, not the last editor or a full change history.
style.creator.precedence: Fixed at creation and unaffected by later participation from the other party.
examples: A browser-created entry remains User after an Agent edits it.
nonExamples: The party that most recently changed the description.

style.creator-all.meaning: Show both User-created and Agent-created style entries without restricting the creator.
style.creator-all.scope: The neutral creator filter option in the style library.
style.creator-all.precedence: A filter state, not a creator value stored on an entry.
examples: Display User and Agent entries together.
nonExamples: Create an entry with All as its creator.

style.creator-user.meaning: The immutable marker for a style entry originally created through the browser by the user.
style.creator-user.scope: Style preview-header markers and the creator filter.
style.creator-user.precedence: Peer to Agent; later Agent edits do not alter it.
examples: A user pastes references and saves the new style in the browser.
nonExamples: An entry first created by an Agent and later edited by a user.

style.creator-agent.meaning: The immutable marker for a style entry originally created through the Agent CLI.
style.creator-agent.scope: Style preview-header markers and the creator filter.
style.creator-agent.precedence: Peer to User; later user edits do not alter it.
examples: An Agent saves a useful style it collected.
nonExamples: A User entry that an Agent later updates.

style.references.meaning: The ordered group of zero or more original images that visually demonstrate one style.
style.references.scope: The left side of style preview and the reference-image controls in create/edit flows.
style.references.referent: PNG, JPEG, or WebP reference images attached directly to the style entry.
style.references.precedence: Visual evidence interpreted alongside the complete design specification.
examples: Three screenshots demonstrating one UI style.

style.description.meaning: The complete design specification an Agent follows when processing a canvas or modeling in a consumer project.
style.description.scope: The right side of style preview and the single description control in create/edit flows. Includes 3D modeling specifications consumed alongside spatial guidance.
style.description.referent: One required free-text specification, which may contain principles, rules, examples, and constraints.
style.description.precedence: Explicit user content, function and approximate spatial intent bound its application; the short prompt summary is only a delivery excerpt.
examples: Preserve asymmetric balance, generous whitespace, strong type scale contrast and restrained geometric accents.
nonExamples: A promotional introduction without design guidance.

style.search.meaning: Filter the local style collection by text found in the management name or overall description.
style.search.scope: The search control above the style-card collection.
style.search.referent: Already persisted style entries in the current library.
style.search.precedence: Combines with category and creator filters; it does not search external sources.
examples: Search for monochrome across style names and descriptions.
nonExamples: Ask an Agent to collect styles from the internet.

style.delete.meaning: Permanently remove one style entry together with all of its reference images, without archiving it.
style.delete.scope: The destructive confirmation opened from a style preview.
style.delete.referent: The currently previewed style entry and its stored reference images.
style.delete.precedence: Permanent terminal action; distinct from removing only one reference image.
examples: Delete a style and every image attached to it.
nonExamples: Remove one reference image while keeping the style.

style.empty.meaning: A library or current filter result contains no style entries to display.
style.empty.referent: Either the whole style library or the currently filtered subset.
style.empty.precedence: The filtered variant applies only when persisted entries exist outside the current filters.
examples: Show an empty state before the first style is created.
nonExamples: The left preview panel for a style with no reference images.

style.operation-status.meaning: Concise progress or failure feedback for loading and mutating style-library data.
style.operation-status.scope: The style-library loading boundary and specific operation errors; generic mutation failures use errors.operationFailed and recovery controls use actions.retry.
style.operation-status.referent: Local style API requests, including list, save, delete, and image upload operations.
style.operation-status.precedence: Operational feedback only; it is not persisted style content.
examples: Show failure feedback after the style list request fails.
nonExamples: The overall description stored on a style entry.

style.prompt-summary.meaning: One concise sentence expressing the distinctive visual traits appended to copied prompts.
style.prompt-summary.scope: Style library and composition/UI session style controls and exports.
style.prompt-summary.referent: One concise sentence expressing the distinctive visual traits appended to copied prompts.
style.prompt-summary.precedence: User intent governs style application; this concept is distinct from the complete specification and from canvas content.
examples: Restrained spacing, bold type contrast and a few geometric accents.

style.session-binding.meaning: The optional single style selected for the current composition, UI or spatial session and shared with its Agent.
style.session-binding.scope: Shared style controls for composition, UI and spatial sessions.
style.session-binding.referent: The optional single style selected for the current composition, UI or spatial session and shared with its Agent.
style.session-binding.precedence: User intent governs style application; this concept is distinct from the complete specification and from canvas content.
examples: Use the selected monochrome style while processing this UI canvas.
Bind a modeling style to spatial guidance for implementation in a consumer project; binding does not modify the scene.

style.session-unbind.meaning: Remove the current session style binding while retaining canvas content.
style.session-unbind.scope: Shared style controls for composition, UI and spatial sessions.
style.session-unbind.referent: Remove the current session style binding while retaining canvas content.
style.session-unbind.precedence: User intent governs style application; this concept is distinct from the complete specification and from canvas content.
examples: Clear the selected style from one session.

style.session-select.meaning: Bind the currently previewed style to the active session.
style.session-select.scope: Shared style controls for composition, UI and spatial sessions.
style.session-select.referent: Bind the currently previewed style to the active session.
style.session-select.precedence: User intent governs style application; this concept is distinct from the complete specification and from canvas content.
examples: Select this style and return to the canvas.

style.session-pending.meaning: The current canvas has not been processed with the selected style revision.
style.session-pending.scope: Style library and composition/UI session style controls and exports.
style.session-pending.referent: The current canvas has not been processed with the selected style revision.
style.session-pending.precedence: User intent governs style application; this concept is distinct from the complete specification and from canvas content.
examples: A newly bound or updated style requires another Agent processing pass.
nonExamples: Whether an external consumer project has finished modeling from a spatial session.

style.session-conflict.meaning: The session or style changed while an operation was in progress; reload before retrying.
style.session-conflict.scope: Shared style controls for composition, UI and spatial sessions.
style.session-conflict.referent: The session or style changed while an operation was in progress; reload before retrying.
style.session-conflict.precedence: User intent governs style application; this concept is distinct from the complete specification and from canvas content.
examples: The user switched styles while the Agent was processing.

style.category-spatial.meaning: A reusable specification of 3D shape language, proportions, materials, palette, lighting and camera treatment for modeling in a consumer project.
style.category-spatial.scope: Style-library category filters, preview markers and creation/editing controls; the default filter for spatial session style selection.
style.category-spatial.referent: The spatial style category, not a spatial session, a character appearance switch or a stored mesh asset.
style.category-spatial.precedence: Peer to Visual and UI. Explicit user constraints and authored spatial requirements govern implementation when style preferences conflict.
examples: A low-poly toy-city style with matte materials and simplified proportions.
nonExamples: Switching a pose guide to geometric appearance.

styleLibrary.title.role: page title and top-level navigation label

styleLibrary.newStyle.role: primary creation action and creation dialog title

styleLibrary.editStyle.role: edit action and edit dialog title

styleLibrary.namePlaceholder.role: placeholder for the style name input

styleLibrary.category.all.role: category filter option that applies no restriction

styleLibrary.category.ui.duplicateReason: It intentionally matches existing UI labels while naming the style category rather than an editor or session.

styleLibrary.creator.all.role: creator filter option that applies no restriction

styleLibrary.creator.user.role: immutable User creator badge and filter option

styleLibrary.creator.agent.role: immutable Agent creator badge and filter option
styleLibrary.creator.agent.duplicateReason: It intentionally matches other Agent labels while identifying the immutable creator of a style entry.

styleLibrary.references.heading.role: heading for the left preview content panel

styleLibrary.references.empty.role: empty state when a style has no reference images

styleLibrary.references.add.role: action that chooses local reference images

styleLibrary.references.remove.role: accessible name for removing one selected reference image

styleLibrary.references.pasteHint.role: short on-demand instruction inside the image collection control

styleLibrary.references.fileTypes.role: supported reference-image file types and size limit

styleLibrary.description.heading.role: heading for the right preview panel and label for the only description field

styleLibrary.description.placeholder.role: placeholder for the one overall description input

styleLibrary.searchPlaceholder.role: placeholder and accessible name for local style search

styleLibrary.deleteTitle.role: title of the permanent style deletion confirmation

styleLibrary.deleteDescription.role: description of the content permanently removed with a style

styleLibrary.empty.role: empty state before any style exists

styleLibrary.noMatches.role: empty state for filters with no matching entries

styleLibrary.loading.role: accessible loading label for the style collection

styleLibrary.save.role: primary action that persists the create or edit form

styleLibrary.imageInvalid.role: validation error for a pasted or selected unsupported image

styleLibrary.openStyle.role: accessible name for opening a named style preview
styleLibrary.openStyle.grammar: imperative verb phrase with a style-name placeholder

styleLibrary.closePreview.role: accessible name for closing the style preview

sessionStyle.prompt.role: one style instruction in an exported prompt

styleLibrary.description.spatialPlacehol.role: placeholder for the full 3D modeling specification
